## Screens, apps and children's reading

In 2025, more than one in five UK 8- to 18-year-olds read fiction on a screen at least monthly [@pictonTrendsChildrenYoung2026].

```{=typst}
#linked-image("figures/evidence.svg", "figures/evidence-links.json")
```

::: {.caption}
Italic rows give findings without a pooled g or d. In the other rows, k is the number of comparisons pooled.
:::

::: {.takeaway}
Plain screens cost about 0.2 SD of comprehension, with no clear cost for narratives. Add-ons help when they serve the story, and ed-tech gains shrink on standardised tests.
:::

### Where the research has looked

Research on children's digital reading has studied devices and add-ons far more than the language of the text or log data.

```{=typst}
#image("figures/scopus.svg")
```

::: {.caption}
Scopus records matching each search, counted on 14 October 2026 with the scopusflow package [@bernabeuScopusflowCRAN2026]. AI's share doubled, yet we found no meta-analysis of generative AI and children's reading.
:::


## *Let's Story*: AI stories, logged at scale

In this app feature, a child picks a hero, companion, setting, plot and theme. A generative model then writes the story [@ratnerDidRobotWrite2025]. In its first month, *Let's Story* logged 419,700 sessions in 18 languages [@ratnerProductiveStruggleChildrens2026].

## Six confirmatory hypotheses

We test whether text features that slow or speed reading in the laboratory do the same in the app.

```{=typst}
#image("figures/model.svg")
```

::: {.caption}
A plus sign predicts slower reading, a minus sign faster. H2 and H3 are `#box[two-sided]`{=typst} because rival accounts predict opposite signs. The analysis covers two age bands (7–8 and 9+) and ten of the app's languages.
:::

## Precision comes from stories, not sessions

```{=typst}
#image("figures/precision.svg")
```

::: {.caption}
Chance that a 0.10 SD effect is judged non-negligible (95% interval outside ±0.05 SD), simulated with the pilotr package [@bernabeuPilotrCRAN2026]. A main effect needs `r req$main_lo`–`r req$main_hi` distinct stories, or about `r req$bf_main` under the registered `#box[Bayes-factor]`{=typst} rule. Assumed: one reading per child, 9% of the variance between stories and 20% between children, equal age bands, independent text measures, and no language terms, covariates or priors.
:::

::: {.takeaway}
Effects that hold in the app could inform how AI stories are pitched to each age band, though faster reading is not better understanding. Effects that fade may reflect home reading conditions or the measure as much as the theory.
:::
